Both lanes are working. On **http://maker:4001** you'll now see three view buttons — **All / Read later / Archived** — above the search box. Try this:

1. On any bookmark, press **"Read later."** It gets a small **"Read later" flag**, and the **Read later** button's count goes up.
2. Click the **Read later** view button — you now see just those, on their own.
3. Back in **All**, press **"Archive"** on a bookmark you want out of the way. It **disappears from All** immediately — your main view is decluttered.
4. Click the **Archived** view — there it is, safely kept. Press **"Restore to All"** to bring it back.

Two design decisions here that I'd really like your call on:

- **Right now, a "Read later" item still also appears in your main "All" list** (just with a flag), as well as under Read later. I wasn't sure whether you think of "read later" as *"still in my collection, but let me also focus on it separately"* — or as *"take it out of the main list so All stays clean."* Which matches how you picture it? If it's the second, I'll show you that version.
- **Archived items are hidden from All and only turn up in the Archived view** — including when you search. So a search while viewing "All" won't surface archived links; you'd switch to Archived to search those. Does keeping archived links out of your normal searches feel right, or would you want search to reach them too?

How do these two lanes feel?
